{ "name": "jquery.json-viewer", "version": "1.4.0", "description": "jQuery plugin for displaying JSON data", "repository": { "type": "git", "url": "https://github.com/abodelot/jquery.json-viewer.git" }, "keywords": [ "jquery-plugin", "json", "json-viewer", "json2html" ], "author": "Alexandre Bodelot ", "license": "MIT", "bugs": { "url": "https://github.com/abodelot/jquery.json-viewer/issues" }, "homepage": "https://github.com/abodelot/jquery.json-viewer", "scripts": { "lint": "eslint json-viewer test", "test": "jest" }, "devDependencies": { "eslint": "^7.28.0", "eslint-plugin-jest": "^24.3.6", "jest": "^27.0.4", "jquery": "^3.6.0" } } # jQuery json-viewer ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/jquery.json-viewer.svg) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/jquery.json-viewer.svg) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/jquery.json-viewer.svg) *json-viewer* is a jQuery plugin for easily displaying JSON objects by transforming them into HTML. Features: - Syntax highlighting - Collapse and expand child nodes on click - Clickable links - Easily readable and minimal DOM structure Check out the [demo page](http://rawgit.com/abodelot/jquery.json-viewer/master/demo.html)! ## Install With npm: ```sh npm install jquery.json-viewer ``` Make sure jQuery is already included. Then import `jquery.json-viewer.js` and `jquery.json-viewer.css` in your HTML document: ```html ``` You can also simply copy `json-viewer/jquery.json-viewer.js` and `json-viewer/jquery.json-viewer.css` files from this git repository into your project. ## Usage Call the `jsonViewer()` method on target element and pass your JSON data in argument: ```html 

```

```js
var data = {
  "foobar": "foobaz"
};
$('#json-renderer').jsonViewer(data);
```

## Options

The `jsonViewer` method accepts an optional config object as a second argument. The supported options are:

- `collapsed` (boolean, default: `false`): all nodes are collapsed at html generation.
- `rootCollapsable` (boolean, default: `true`): allow root element to be collasped.
- `withQuotes` (boolean, default: `false`): all JSON keys are surrounded with double quotation marks (`{"foobar": 1}` instead of `{foobar: 1}`).
- `withLinks` (boolean, default: `true`): all values that are valid links will be clickable, if `false` they will only be strings.

Example:

```js
$('#json-renderer').jsonViewer(data, {collapsed: true, withQuotes: true, withLinks: false});
```

## About

- Author: [Alexandre Bodelot](https://github.com/abodelot)
- License: [MIT License](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

1.4.0 - Released on 2019-08-19

  * Fixed performance issue with 'withLinks' option
  * Escape double quotes in string values

1.3.0 - Released on 2019-07-04

  * Improved URL detection
  * Fixed XSS injection with 'withLinks' option
  * Fixed JS error when JSON has an attribute 'hasOwnProperty'

1.2.0 - Released on 2019-03-10

  * Added 'rootCollapsable' option
  * Added 'withLinks' option
  * Added 'withQuotes' option
  * Updated to jQuery 3.x
  * Improved style of toggle arrows
  * Fixed JS error in scrict mode

1.1.0 - Released on 2016-02-16

  * Added 'collapsed' option
  * Escape XML/HTML tags in JSON content
  * Made dict key names clickable

1.0.0 - Released on 2015-01-11

  * Initial release

Audit complete. `findings.json` is written in the repo root; no source file was touched (timestamps unchanged). ## Findings **1. XSS via unescaped object keys — `json-viewer/jquery.json-viewer.js:80-87` (CWE-79)** The escaping at lines 33-38 is applied only to string *values*. Object *keys* are concatenated raw into the markup, which then reaches `$(this).html(html)` at line 128. I confirmed this by executing the plugin against a stub jQuery: ``` input : { "": 1 } output:
  • : 1
    • ``` It injects in all three key render paths — bare key (line 86), `withQuotes` span (line 81, where a key of `x">` also breaks the quoted context), and inside the `json-toggle` anchor (line 84). Since the JSON fed to a viewer is typically untrusted, control of any key name gives script execution. The upstream project later fixed exactly this by adding a shared `htmlEscape()` helper applied to keys. **2. Code injection via `eval()` — `demo.html:32-38` (CWE-95)** Textarea content goes to `eval('(' + ... + ')')` instead of `JSON.parse`, so any valid JavaScript runs with page privileges; the `try/catch` only hides errors. `renderJson()` also fires automatically on page load and on every option checkbox click. Delivery requires the JSON to come from someone other than the person typing (a "paste this to reproduce" payload) — but that is the page's purpose, and since this file is the repository's reference usage example, the pattern becomes remotely triggerable in any consumer that feeds it fetched JSON. ## Checked and ruled out - **`javascript:`/`data:` URIs through `withLinks`** (line 41) — I tested `javascript:alert(1)`, mixed-case variants, `data:text/html,...`, and `//evil.com` against the `isUrl` regex; the mandatory `[a-z0-9%-]+\.` segment rejects all of them, and attribute breakout is blocked because `"` and `'` are escaped before the test. - **ReDoS in `isUrl`** — the nested quantifier looks suspicious, but `[a-z0-9%-]+` excludes `.`, so segment splits are deterministic. Timed runs scale linearly (32 KB input in 0.4 ms), so no catastrophic backtracking. - **`target.after(...)`** (line 141) — interpolates only a numeric `.length`. - String values, numbers, booleans, and the array branch are clean; the `hasOwnProperty` guard at line 78 prevents inherited-property injection. One lower-severity item outside the requested categories, noted but not filed: line 41 emits `target="_blank"` with no `rel="noopener"` (reverse tabnabbing, CWE-1022).
